title: US Goes Behind Sheinbaum’s Back – Soberanía 127
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 127 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
open with another case of U.S. interference — this time in Querétaro, where
Governor Mauricio Kuri and Ambassador Ron Johnson broke ground on a police
training academy without federal authorization. The hosts explain how this
violates Mexico's National Security Law, which explicitly requires high-level
federal approval for any security cooperation with foreign governments. They
note the pattern: Chihuahua and now Querétaro, PAN-governed states where the
U.S. is pursuing a "subnational strategy" to work around the federal
government that defends Mexican sovereignty.

Next, they discuss AMLO's return via a video promoting his new book, "Pueblo."
In a wide-ranging 90-minute address, he criticized Ron Johnson as "a meddling
policeman," denounced U.S. hypocrisy on drug trafficking, and dedicated the
book to Claudia Sheinbaum, calling her "the best president in the world" —
definitively debunking the opposition's fantasy of a rift between them.

The conversation then turns to Brazil's presidential election, where Lula and
Flávio Bolsonaro are separated by just two points heading into a runoff. The
hosts analyze the structural challenges facing the Latin American left: late
capitalism, low growth, and a far-right that promises to "get the state off
your back" while offering nothing but nihilism. They note that Brazil's high
abstention rate (over 30 million voters) could be decisive, but warn that
convincing non-voters to turn out is an uphill battle.

Losers and Haters takes aim at Instagram and Meta for removing their video
reporting on Bolsonaro's sex parties and suspicious gifts, claiming it
violated community standards on sexual violence — even though it was
journalistic reporting on a public scandal. The hosts note the irony: the same
platform that briefly suspended Lula's ads is now censoring critical
journalism while allowing fake election-day ads to flourish.
